cross_references.label: Authentication Required for Admission
cross_references.note: §1401 states that a writing is not admissible unless it is authenticated. §1400 defines what authentication means; §1401 makes authentication a prerequisite for admission. Both sections must be cited together when objecting to admission of an unauthenticated writing.

cross_references.label: Means of Authentication
cross_references.note: §§1410-1421 provide the specific methods by which a writing may be authenticated: handwriting evidence, comparison writing, expert opinion, distinctive characteristics, authentication by reply, official seals, etc. These are the tools for satisfying §1400(a).

cross_references.label: Self-Authenticating Documents
cross_references.note: §§1450-1454 list categories of documents that are self-authenticating and do not require extrinsic evidence under §1400(a). Official records, certified copies, and other enumerated categories are authenticated by their form and origin.

cross_references.label: Business Records Exception
cross_references.note: §1271 provides an authentication pathway for business records. A writing that qualifies as a business record under §1271 is authenticated through that section's foundation requirements (regular course of business, contemporaneous recording, personal knowledge). §1400 is satisfied once §1271's requirements are met.

cross_references.label: Official Records Exception
cross_references.note: §1280 provides an authentication pathway for official government records. A document purporting to be an official record must be authenticated under §1400 — and §1280 provides the foundation elements. Failure to establish §1280 foundation means §1400 is not satisfied.

cross_references.label: Computer Printouts
cross_references.note: §1552 provides a presumption for computer-generated printouts and electronically stored information. The §1400 authentication framework applies to electronic records; §1552 provides a specific pathway for establishing that a computer printout reflects the data in the computer at the relevant time.

cross_references.label: Federal Rules of Evidence — Authentication
cross_references.note: FRE 901 is the federal analog to §1400 in federal court proceedings. The standard is similar — evidence sufficient to support a finding. Federal cases involving similar authentication questions are persuasive authority in California state court proceedings.
